titleEn: The psychology that can lead investors to make bad financial decisions
titleZh: 哪些心理机制，会让投资者作出糟糕的财务决定？
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Say you buy shares in a company. The price climbs and months later you sell for a healthy profit. Ask why it worked, and the answer is often some version of “I made a good call”. Now imagine the trade had lost money instead. Would you be as quick to blame your own judgment? Many of us wouldn’t. We may point to bad timing, a jittery market, anything but ourselves.
paragraphs.zh: 假设你买入了一家公司的股票。股价上涨，几个月后你卖出股票，获得了可观的利润。当被问到为什么这样做会成功时，答案往往是“我做了一个正确的判断”。现在，想象一下，这笔交易反而亏了钱。你会这么快就责怪自己的判断吗？我们中的许多人不会。我们可能会指出时机不对，市场动荡，除了我们自己以外的任何事情。

paragraphs.en: Psychologists call this “self-attribution bias”. Crediting ourselves for good outcomes, blaming something else for bad ones.
paragraphs.zh: 心理学家称之为“自我归因偏见”，把好的结果归功于自己，而把坏的结果归咎于别人。

paragraphs.en: This bias matters more now that trading apps have made it easier for people with no formal training in finance to manage their own investments. Many of these apps offer tax-efficient accounts, such as stocks and shares Isas and self-invested personal pensions. They promote the tax advantages alongside low fees and sign-up incentives.
paragraphs.zh: 这种偏见现在变得更加重要，因为交易应用让没有受过正规金融培训的人更容易管理自己的投资。许多这类应用提供节税账户，比如股票和股份个人退休账户（Isas）以及自我投资的个人养老金账户。它们在宣传低费用和注册激励的同时，还宣传税收优势。

paragraphs.en: My colleagues and I explore this in our latest study, which examines self-attribution alongside two related biases – overconfidence and loss aversion – among people training to work in finance.
paragraphs.zh: 我和我的同事在我们最新的研究中探讨了这一点，该研究考察了接受金融工作培训的人的自我归因以及两种相关偏见-过度自信和损失厌恶。

paragraphs.en: Behavioural finance exists as a subject because traditional theory, which assumes investors act rationally, struggles to explain why markets are prone to bubbles, or why we cling to losing positions long after we should sell. Self-attribution, overconfidence (an inflated sense of our ability relative to others) and loss aversion (feeling a loss more keenly than an equivalent gain) sit at the centre of it.
paragraphs.zh: 行为金融学之所以成为一门学科，是因为传统理论（假定投资者理性行事）难以解释为什么市场容易出现泡沫，或者为什么我们在应该卖出的很长时间后仍坚持持有亏损头寸。自我归因、过度自信（对自己相对于他人的能力的一种夸大感）和损失厌恶（对损失的感觉比同等收益更强烈）是行为金融学的核心。

paragraphs.en: It’s a subject now taught at more than 40 UK universities. Yet there’s been surprisingly little research into teaching students to recognise these biases in their own decisions, rather than just learning the theory.
paragraphs.zh: 目前，英国有40多所大学开设了这门课程。然而，令人惊讶的是，除了学习理论之外，很少有研究教学生认识到自己决策中的这些偏见。

paragraphs.en: Knowledge doesn’t make us immune
paragraphs.zh: 知识并不能让我们免疫

paragraphs.en: We studied the financial decisions of 72 postgraduate students taking an MSc in finance and investment at the University of South Wales. They came from a range of countries, mainly Nigeria, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. Most were in their 30s or older. About 40% had never traded with real money.
paragraphs.zh: 我们研究了72名在南威尔士大学（University of South Wales）攻读金融与投资硕士学位的研究生的财务决策。他们来自不同的国家，主要是尼日利亚、斯里兰卡和孟加拉国。大多数人年龄在30多岁或以上。约40%的人从未用真实的货币进行过交易。

paragraphs.en: Over four weeks, the students learned about trading psychology and then took part in a series of simulated trading exercises. This research project ended with a final trading game that counted towards their assessment. They also completed questionnaires and looked back at their own trading decisions to identify possible biases.
paragraphs.zh: 在四周的时间里，学生们学习了交易心理学，然后参加了一系列模拟交易练习。这个研究项目以一个最终的交易游戏结束，这个游戏计入了他们的评估。他们还完成了问卷调查，并回顾了自己的交易决策，以确定可能的偏见。

paragraphs.en: Before the final trading game, we asked students how well they expected to perform. Afterwards, we asked whether their actual result reflected their own trading skill. The difference was striking. More than 80% of students who performed better than expected said their result reflected their skill.
paragraphs.zh: 在最后的交易游戏之前，我们问学生他们期望的表现如何。之后，我们问他们的实际结果是否反映了他们自己的交易技能。差异是惊人的。超过80%的学生表现好于预期，他们的结果反映了他们的技能。

paragraphs.en: Among those who performed worse than expected, only about 16% said the same. Overall, nearly 70% of students acknowledged that they tended to take more credit for success than for failure.
paragraphs.zh: 在那些表现比预期差的学生中，只有大约16%的人说同样的话。总体而言，近70%的学生承认，他们倾向于把更多的功劳归于成功，而不是失败。

paragraphs.en: We also found signs of overconfidence. For example, 84% of students expected to finish in the top half of the group, even though, by definition, no more than half could do so. Even among students who said they rarely followed financial news, everyone rated their understanding of it as at least “fair”.
paragraphs.zh: 我们还发现了过度自信的迹象。例如，84%的学生期望在小组中排名前一半，尽管根据定义，不超过一半的学生可以做到这一点。即使在那些说他们很少关注财经新闻的学生中，每个人都认为他们对财经新闻的理解至少是“一般”。

paragraphs.en: We also found evidence of loss aversion. Students were asked to imagine two coin flips, risking £25 on one and £100 on the other, and named the smallest prize that would make each worth playing. Across both flips, around 75% asked for more than they stood to lose (indicating loss aversion), broadly in line with findings from research involving people in 53 countries.
paragraphs.zh: 我们还发现了厌恶损失的证据。学生们被要求想象两次抛硬币，一次风险为25英镑，另一次风险为100英镑，并说出每一次都值得玩的最小奖品。在两次抛硬币中，大约75%的人要求比他们失去的更多（表明厌恶损失），这与涉及53个国家的人的研究结果大致一致。

paragraphs.en: It would be reassuring to think people studying for a finance masters – several with real trading experience already – would be less susceptible to these bases. Our results suggest otherwise.
paragraphs.zh: 如果我们认为攻读金融硕士的人--其中有几个已经有了真实的交易经验--不太容易受到这些基础的影响，那就令人放心了。

paragraphs.en: That does not prove financial knowledge makes no difference. We did not compare this group with people who had no financial background. And we measured them once, not as their expertise grew as time progressed.
paragraphs.zh: 这并不能证明金融知识没有影响。我们没有将这组人与没有金融背景的人进行比较。我们只对他们进行了一次测量，而不是随着他们的专业知识随着时间的推移而增长。

paragraphs.en: But it does show that technical, theoretical knowledge of markets was not, by itself, enough to stop these tendencies appearing. These biases are not really about what you know. They are about how the mind processes wins, losses and uncertainty, often automatically, before conscious reasoning gets a look in.
paragraphs.zh: 但它确实表明，市场的技术和理论知识本身并不足以阻止这些倾向的出现，这些偏见并不真正关乎你所知道的，而是关乎大脑如何在有意识的推理出现之前自动处理输赢和不确定性。

paragraphs.en: So what can investors do?
paragraphs.zh: 那么，投资者可以做些什么呢？

paragraphs.en: There was, however, an encouraging sign after a structured sequence of exercises, comparing predictions against outcomes, reviewing their own trading data and reflecting on decisions. The self-rated understanding of all three biases by students improved significantly.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，经过一系列结构化的练习，比较预测与结果，回顾自己的交易数据并反思决策，学生们对所有三种偏见的自我评估理解明显提高。

paragraphs.en: It is important to note that this measured how well students felt they understood the biases, not their actual knowledge or behaviour. Feeling more aware of a bias is not the same as reliably avoiding it. As the study itself notes, insight is a start, but it doesn’t guarantee different decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 值得注意的是，这一研究衡量的是学生们对偏见的理解程度，而不是他们的实际知识或行为。感觉更了解偏见并不等同于可靠地避免偏见。正如研究本身所指出的，洞察力是一个开始，但它并不保证不同的决定。

paragraphs.en: None of this means investors are doomed to be led astray by their own psychology, but simply knowing the theory isn’t enough. What seemed to help our students was structure. In other words, writing down what they expected before deciding, then honestly comparing it with what happened, reviewing their own trading history for patterns rather than trusting memory, and also setting rules for buying and selling in advance, not in the heat of the moment.
paragraphs.zh: 这并不意味着投资者注定会被自己的心理引入歧途，但仅仅知道理论是不够的。似乎对我们的学生有帮助的是结构。换句话说，在决定之前写下他们的预期，然后诚实地将其与发生的事情进行比较，回顾自己的交易历史以寻找模式，而不是相信记忆，并且提前设定买卖规则，不是一时冲动

paragraphs.en: None of that requires a finance degree. For anyone managing their own pension or investments, the lesson may be simple – be wary of any story where your wins are always down to skill and your losses always down to bad luck.
paragraphs.zh: 所有这些都不需要金融学位。对于任何管理自己养老金或投资的人来说，教训可能很简单--警惕任何胜利总是归功于技能而失败总是归咎于运气不好的故事。
